newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Vranitzky says he will not step down.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Vranitzky says he will not step down.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky will not step down, despite his Social Democratic Party's dismal showing in European parliamentary polls on Sunday, Der Standard newspaper reported on Wednesday.

In an interview Vranitzky, chancellor for the past 10 years, said he would remain in office until Austria's next scheduled general elections in 1999 and he refused to shoulder the entire blame for his party's worst performance since 1918.
"I am not shirking any responsibility but I will not take the entire blame," Der Standard quoted Vranitzky as saying.

Asked if he would stay on as chancellor and Social Democrat party leader until 1999, he replied with an emphatic "Yes" and denied he was eyeing the Austrian presidency or a job at the European Commission.

The Social Democrats scored just 29.1 percent in Sunday's vote, falling behind junior coalition partners the People's Party for the first time in 30 years. The far-right Freedom Party of Joerg Haider won a record 27.6 percent.

Vranitzky, a former banker, traced his party's decline in the polls to a low turnout among Social Democrat voters and widespread disenchantment with a two-year austerity budget, passed by parliament in March.

"Unions and some regional party bosses spent a lot of time chewing over the budget and that made things difficult for us," he said, pointing the finger at his critics within the Social Democratic movement.

Vranitzky reiterated that there would be no ministerial reshuffle in the immediate future but hinted that he planned social reforms to ease public concerns about unemployment and crime -- two vote winners for Haider.
He accused the populist leader of wanting an isolated and inward-looking Austria, reminiscent of the Cold War years when the Alpine republic was sandwiched between East and West.
